text:
ajohnson: heads up — after last night's kernel + CUDA roll (kernel 6.6 -> 6.7, cuda 12.2 -> 12.3) a subset of mixed-sku racks are failing NVLink peer discovery and we're seeing automatic SHM/NET/socket fallbacks. 20-40% perf hit on short-seq generation.

mli: saw the alerts early morning, thanks. symptoms?

ajohnson: logs show nccl marking P2P unavailable, then switching to NET. example: 
```
NCCL INFO Topology: peer (node-3:GPU1) NVLink probe failed: -3
NCCL WARN P2P: NVLink not detected, falling back to NET
NCCL INFO Using socket transport between ranks
```

sre_maria: are these mixed H100/A100 racks or all one SKU?

ajohnson: mixed racks — NVIDIA driver 535.x on A100s, 540.x on H100s (we rolled drivers per-region). suspect mismatch + kernel change.

ops_tam: reproduction steps? can we `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `nccl-tests` on the nodes?

priya: ran quick `nccl-tests` on a bad rack: `all_reduce` throughput down ~30%, `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows NVLink connections but `nccl-tests` still picks socket.

mli: can you paste the `nvidia-smi topo -m` output and driver versions?

ajohnson: pasted below: 
```
# nvidia-smi topo -m
        GPU0    GPU1    CPU
GPU0    X       NVLink  NODE0
GPU1    NVLink  X       NODE0

# /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  540.23.01  Wed Feb  7 14:00:00 UTC 2025
# kernel
Linux rack-node-3 6.7.0-1-custom
```

mli: interesting — topo shows NVLink but NCCL probe fails. could be kernel ABI changes or a module symbol rename. did we change `nvidia-uvm` or secure module signing?

infra-bot: deploy 2025-02-15_cuda-12.3 initiated to region-us-west-2 (tracking ID: dep-3345).

ops_tam: quick workaround: force enable P2P with `NCCL_P2P=1` or disable peer checks? any env flags?

mli: there are envs: `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL` and `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE`. forcing p2p can hang if detection is wrong. safer: set `NCCL_TOPO_DEBUG=INFO` and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and collect logs first.

priya: ran with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` on one failing job, grabbed this snippet: 
```
ncclTopoGetLinkType: linkType NVLINK reported but nvlinkProbe returned -5
ncclP2pSetup: peer check failed, marking NET fallback
```

sre_maria: timeline? which regions got the new kernel/driver?

ajohnson: us-west-2 and eu-central got kernel 6.7 + driver 540 on H100 pools. some leftover A100 racks still on 535 + kernel 6.6 due to reserved capacity. mixed-sku scheduling caused cross-sku jobs to run.

ops_tam: pragmatic plan: 1) pin scheduling to homogeneous racks while we triage, 2) roll back driver on a small test rack to confirm, 3) open ticket with NVIDIA if repro. agree?

mli: +1. also add a temporary admission controller that prevents mixing different driver versions in the same job.

ajohnson: started a cordon for 3 affected racks, and applied a scheduler label to avoid cross-placement.

priya: did a quick rollback on a single rack (H100) to driver 535 & kernel 6.6 — ran nccl-tests, NVLink P2P restored, perf back to baseline.

sre_maria: good repro signal. please capture kernel logs and `dmesg` around module load, and send to NVIDIA.

ajohnson: `dmesg` snippet: 
```
[  12.345678] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[  12.346000] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: nvlink_probe: returned -22
[  12.346500] nvidia-uvm: loaded
```

mli: sounds like probe ABI mismatch or a kernel helper missing. ticket to NVIDIA with: kernel version, driver version, nvlink logs, `modinfo nvidia`, `uname -a`, and sample `nccl` logs. I'll draft.

ops_tam: in parallel: can infra add a rollout guard to avoid mixing driver versions during upgrades? maybe use a staged canary with homogenous racks only.

ajohnson: created runbook checklist in the ops playbook and added scheduler guard. also queued a rollback for the remaining H100 racks pending NVIDIA response.

infra-bot: incident created: INC-2025-042 — NVLINK probe regressions after kernel/driver upgrade. severity: P2. assignees: ajohnson, mli.

priya: one note: some short-seq workloads are more sensitive due to low token batching — we should update perf tests to include 1-8 token seq distrib to catch regressions early.

mli: agreed — adding short-seq smoke to the upgrade pipeline.

sre_maria: thanks team. next update in 2 hours or when NVIDIA responds. :raised_hands:
